> At the sample level, participants were excluded based on low call rate, abnormal heterozygosity, and non-European ancestry.

> Genes with overall mean expression > 15 reads and expressed in at least 5% of the participants were retained for further analysis.

> Following quality control and merging with genomic and imaging data, 1,891 participants were included in the downstream eQTL and gene-expression association analyses.

> In the Rhineland Study, among the first 5,500 participants enrolled before April 2020, 2,852 were selected using age-and sex-stratified random sampling for proteomics analysis.

> Following quality control and merging with genomic and imaging data, 2,299 participants were included in the downstream OLINK-based pQTL and protein association analyses.

> Among participants enrolled in the Rhineland Study before November 26, 2021, 551 were selected randomly after stratifying by age and sex, creating a random representative subset of the entire cohort.

> Following quality control and merging with genomic and imaging data, 376 participants were included in the downstream SEER-based pQTL and protein association analyses.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report: No power analyses were detected.

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

table.header: Two-sample Mendelian Randomization
table.expanded: In the forward MR analysis, the primary inverse-variance weighted (IVW) analysis showed that smaller mammillary body volume was associated with an increased risk of MDD, although the association did not reach statistical significance (IVW: β = -0.026, SE = 0.019, P = 0.176).

table.expanded: After excluding outlier SNPs identified by radial MR, the association became statistically significant (IVW: β = -0.037, SE = 0.012, P = 1.72 × 10 ³, FDR-adjusted P = 0.012), indicating that a decrease in mammillary body volume was associated with an increased risk of MDD.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list("P-Value" = c("p < 0.05", "P < 0.05", "P < 2.66", 
"p < 0.05"), Text = c("Gene sets were considered significant if at least two input genes overlapped with the tested gene set and survived Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.05.", 
"In the independent Rhineland Study cohort, 20 lead SNPs representing 20 genomic risk loci identified in the discovery cohort showed directional consistency and nominal replication (P < 0.05) (Table 1, Figure 1B, Supplementary Table 2).", 
"In addition, MAGMA gene-based analysis identified 47 genes that reached gene-wide significance (P < 2.66 × 10 ) (Supplementary Table 15).", 
"Mediation analysis revealed that the effect of 104 SNPs on mammillary body volume were significantly mediated through MEI1 expression (indirect p < 0.05, FDR < 0.02), with the absolute ratio of the indirect effect of the total effect size ranging from 78% to over 100%."
)), row.names = c(NA, -4L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"
))

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, c(0.1, 0.9), 2, FALSE)
```

table.header: Two-sample Mendelian Randomization
table.expanded: In the forward MR analysis, the primary inverse-variance weighted (IVW) analysis showed that smaller mammillary body volume was associated with an increased risk of MDD, although the association did not reach statistical significance (IVW: β = -0.026, SE = 0.019, P = 0.176).

table.header: Two-sample Mendelian Randomization
table.expanded: Significant heterogeneity was detected among the genetic instruments (Cochran's Q = 107.35, P = 1.56 × 10 ).

table.header: Two-sample Mendelian Randomization
table.expanded: After excluding outlier SNPs identified by radial MR, the association became statistically significant (IVW: β = -0.037, SE = 0.012, P = 1.72 × 10 ³, FDR-adjusted P = 0.012), indicating that a decrease in mammillary body volume was associated with an increased risk of MDD.

table.header: Two-sample Mendelian Randomization
table.expanded: In the reverse MR analysis, a higher genetic liability to MDD was also associated with smaller mammillary body volume following removal of outlier SNPs (IVW: β = -0.10, SE = 0.03, P = 1.75 × 10 ³, FDR-adjusted P = 0.01).

stat_p_nonsig.report:
Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is 'no effect', 'no difference', or that groups are 'the same' after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is 'not significantly' different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.
#### Careless Responding
No file could be screened for careless responding.

**What this does not cover.** Only 0 of 4 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.
